changes.title: Amazon EC2 C8gn instances are now available in AWS Israel (Tel Aviv) region
changes.detail: Starting today, Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2) C8gn instances, powered by the latest-generation AWS Graviton4 processors, are available in the AWS Israel (Tel Aviv) region. The C8gn instances provide up to 30% better compute performance than Graviton3-based Amazon EC2 C7gn instances. Amazon EC2 C8gn instances feature the latest 6th generation AWS Nitro Cards, and offer up to 600 Gbps network bandwidth, the highest network bandwidth among network optimized EC2 instances. changes.title: Amazon EC2 C8ine instances are now available in AWS Europe (Ireland) region
changes.detail: Starting today, Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2) C8ine instances are available in the AWS Europe (Ireland) region. C8ine instances are powered by custom sixth generation Intel Xeon Scalable processors, available only on AWS. These instances feature the latest sixth generation AWS Nitro cards, delivering up to 43% higher performance compared to previous generation C6in instances. changes.title: Amazon S3 adds post-quantum TLS key exchange support to additional S3 endpoints
changes.detail: Amazon S3 adds post-quantum TLS (PQ-TLS) key exchange support to S3 Vectors and AWS PrivateLink for Amazon S3 interface endpoints. This extends the post-quantum cryptography support already available on regional S3, S3 Tables, and S3 Express One Zone endpoints. S3 Vectors endpoints and PrivateLink interface endpoints now support Module-Lattice-Based Key-Encapsulation Mechanism (ML-KEM), one of the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) standardized post-quantum cryptographic algorithms. changes.title: Amazon S3 now provides post-quantum TLS visibility in AWS CloudTrail
changes.detail: Amazon S3 now records the TLS key exchange algorithm in AWS CloudTrail for S3 requests, so you can see which requests and clients use post-quantum TLS (PQ-TLS). With this visibility, you can measure the share of your S3 traffic that is protected with post-quantum cryptography, and identify the applications, SDK versions, and IAM principals that still connect with classical key exchange and need to be upgraded.
